newsitem.title: UK: Major welcomes quick restart to N Ireland talks.
newsitem.headline: Major welcomes quick restart to N Ireland talks.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Wednesday welcomed plans to restart multi-party peace talks on Northern Ireland soon after Britain's forthcoming general election and urged the IRA once more to lay down its arms.

Major issued a statement shortly after former U.S. Senator George Mitchell, the chairman of the talks, said they would be adjourned until June 3. The election is widely expected to take place on May 1.
"I welcome agreement that the talks should be rapidly resumed after the general election and the local elections in Northern Ireland," the statement said.
"The talks are the best means available to achieve the comprehensive political settlement so desperately needed.
"I hope that when they resume, all the parties will be ready to make rapid progress on the substantive political issues. I will do all I can to make this possible," he added.

Meanwhile, Major called on the Irish Republican Army (IRA), fighting to end British rule in Northern Ireland, to abandon what he called "futile violence" and renew a ceasefire it broke more than a year ago "credibly and verifiably".
"This would enable the talks to proceed in a peaceful environment and open the opportunity for all parties to participate," Major said.
The Belfast talks were suspended after nine months of deadlock to allow the province's Protestant and Catholic parties to prepare for the British election.

Britain and the Republic of Ireland launched the talks last June in a bid to defuse conflict about British rule. But they have been plagued by acrimony between the parties and overshadowed by growing IRA guerrilla violence.
Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, is barred from the talks because the guerrillas are waging an escalating campaign to unite the largely Protestant province with Catholic Ireland.
